title: Answer every new Google review without posting anything you haven't read
one_liner: Each new Google review lands in your Slack or inbox with a short reply already drafted in your voice. You tap approve or edit, and only then does it go live.
steps: Create a sheet with your business name, how you sign off, and a few phrases you like and never use.
Your automation tool checks Google Business Profile for new reviews that have no owner reply yet.
An AI step drafts a short, specific reply and tags the review as praise, mixed or complaint.
The draft goes to you in Slack or email with the review text and Approve and Edit options; complaints are flagged so you read them first.
After you approve, the reply is posted and the review and reply are logged in the sheet.
guardrail: Nothing is posted until a person approves it, and complaints are never answered by the AI alone.
tools: Google Business Profile, Zapier, Make or n8n, Slack or Gmail, Google Sheets, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT)
prompt:
You draft public replies to Google reviews for a small local business. Use only the facts below.

Business: [business name]
Owner sign-off: [e.g. 'Maria, owner']
Voice notes: [e.g. warm, plain, no exclamation marks]
Words or phrases to avoid: [list]
Star rating: [1-5]
Reviewer first name: [name]
Review text: [paste review]

Write:
1. A reply of 2 to 4 sentences. Thank the reviewer by first name, mention one specific detail they raised, and sign off as given.
2. If the rating is 3 or below, do not apologize for specifics you cannot confirm, do not offer refunds or credits, and invite them to call [phone] or email [email] so you can look into it.
3. A tag on its own line: PRAISE, MIXED or COMPLAINT.
Never invent details about the job, never mention prices, and never reveal private information beyond what the reviewer wrote.
source_name: n8n and Zapier Google review reply templates with Slack approval (search results)
verification_note: Prompt restricts output to supplied facts, fixes length and tag, and forbids invented details, refunds and specifics on low ratings; a model would return a compliant draft.

title: Catch bookings that are missing an address, phone or job detail before the day arrives
one_liner: Every afternoon a check scans tomorrow's bookings for missing details and drafts a short message asking the customer for exactly what is missing, so nobody shows up to an incomplete job.
steps: List the details every booking must have (for example phone, service address, job type, access notes) as columns in your booking sheet or tool.
Each afternoon, your automation tool pulls tomorrow's bookings and checks which required fields are empty.
For each incomplete booking, an AI step drafts a short text or email asking only for the missing items.
You or your office manager get one digest of the drafts and approve them in a batch.
Replies are added to the booking by hand or by your tool, and anything still incomplete the next morning is flagged to a person.
guardrail: Messages go out only after a person approves the batch, and the AI never fills in a missing detail by guessing.
tools: Your booking tool or Google Sheet, Zapier, Make or n8n, Gmail or an SMS tool, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT)
prompt:
You draft short messages asking a customer for missing booking details. Use only the facts below.

Business: [business name]
Customer first name: [first name]
Appointment: [service] on [date] at [time]
Details we already have: [list]
Details still missing: [e.g. service address, gate code]
Channel: [text or email]
Sender name: [name]

Write one message: friendly, under 50 words for text or under 90 words for email, ask only for the missing items as a short list, say why we need them in one clause, and ask them to reply before [deadline].
Do not ask for anything not in the missing list, do not request payment or card details, and do not change the appointment time.
source_name: Zapier missing-booking-information daily check templates (search results)
verification_note: Prompt is scoped to the missing list, bans payment requests and schedule changes, and sets length limits; a model would return a compact on-task message.

title: Find finished jobs that never got an invoice
one_liner: Every Friday, a check compares completed jobs against invoices sent and lists any job that is done but not billed, so money doesn't sit uncollected because someone forgot.
steps: Make sure your job log and your invoice list each carry a shared job or customer ID, in a sheet or your field-service and accounting tools.
Every Friday, your automation tool pulls jobs marked complete in the last 30 days and the invoices issued for the same period.
It matches them and lists completed jobs with no matching invoice.
An AI step turns the list into a short owner email with the job, customer, date and a one-line reason to check, plus a suggested note for whoever bills.
A person confirms each job (some may be warranty or no-charge) and sends or voids the invoice; the sheet records the outcome.
guardrail: The AI only reports mismatches; a person decides whether each job should be billed, and no invoice is created or sent automatically.
tools: Jobber, Housecall Pro or a Google Sheet job log, QuickBooks or your invoicing tool, Zapier, Make or n8n, Gmail, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT)
prompt:
You prepare a Friday email for a small business owner about completed jobs that have no invoice. Use only the rows below.

Business: [business name]
Today: [date]
Completed jobs with no matching invoice (job ID, customer, job type, completion date, assigned to):
[paste rows]

Write:
1. A one-sentence opener stating how many jobs are unbilled.
2. A table sorted oldest first with job ID, customer, job type, days since completion.
3. For jobs older than [14] days, add the note 'Check first: older than [14] days'.
4. A closing line: 'Confirm each job before billing; some may be warranty or no-charge.'
Do not guess amounts, do not say a customer owes money, and if the list is empty write 'No unbilled completed jobs this week.'
source_name: n8n and Zapier missing-payment and unbilled-booking alert templates (search results)
verification_note: Prompt works only from pasted rows, fixes the table and empty-list behaviour and forbids guessing amounts; a model would return a compliant summary.
